newsitem.title: USA: Sepracor allergy drug test is promising.
newsitem.headline: Sepracor allergy drug test is promising.

text.p: Sepracor Inc said Monday that a Phase II study of norastemizole, its non-sedating antihistamine drug candidate, showed treatment at 20- and 62.5-milligram doses resulted in statistically significant improvements in allergic symptoms, compared with a placebo.
In the Phase II double-blind trial, patients received five-, 20- or 62.5-mg doses of norastemizole or a placebo for a two-day period.

Acording to Sepracor, norastemizole treatment at the two higher doses resulted in statistically significant improvements in allergic symptoms, including rhinorrhea, sneezing, itchy eyes and nose, and scratchy throat.
Additionally, there were no differences in incidence and severity of side effects, including cardiac events, when comparing norastemizole with placebo.
